w:r.w:t: Economic Outlook for OECD Countries
The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) publishes regular assessments of the economic outlook for its member countries. This report covers developments from 2024 to 2025.
Several factors are at play, e.g. inflation, monetary policy & trade tensions. These dynamics impact GDP growth across regions.
As described in the
OECD Economic Surveys
, the fiscal stance has
significantly
shifted since Q3 2024.
The US has seen a marked improvement in employment figures. It's expected that this trend won't reverse in the short term.
Growth reached 3% in 5 member countries, while 8 others recorded declines of approximately 1.2 percentage points compared to the previous 2 quarters.
Key recommendation:
Governments should prioritise fiscal consolidation while maintaining social safety nets.
It should be noted that the aforementioned policies were implemented by member states in order to facilitate growth. The utilisation of these instruments is being monitored.
Trade volumes have recovered since the pandemic
, with intra-OECD trade growing by 4.5 per cent per annum.
Monetary Policy Outlook
Central banks, i.e. the ECB, the Fed and the Bank of Japan, have adopted divergent strategies viz. interest rate adjustments, quantitative easing and forward guidance.
